question: A facilities coordinator pasted a list of twelve depots and asked for a condition summary of each. The reply is well organised and covers nine of them without saying that three are absent. What check would have caught this?
options: A) Comparing the length of this reply against the length of the depot summaries she received in previous months.
B) Asking whether every depot on the list has been covered, and accepting the answer that comes back in reply.
C) Reading the summary closely for depots described in less detail than the others, which suggests thin coverage.
D) Counting the entries in the reply against the twelve depots on the list she supplied in her original request.
correct_answers: D) Counting the entries in the reply against the twelve depots on the list she supplied in her original request.
explanations: Overall length varies with how much there was to report each month, so it is far too coarse a signal to reveal three missing entries.
Asking whether coverage is complete invites the same process that produced the gap to confirm there is no gap.
Thin descriptions signal weak coverage of depots that are present. A depot left out entirely produces no description to notice.
Correct. Omissions leave no mark in the text, so they are only visible when the output is counted back against the input. A list she supplied gives her an exact expected number to check against.
